paragraphs.text: Τότε ὁμοιωθήσεται ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν δέκα παρθένοις, αἵτινες λαβοῦσαι τὰς λαμπάδας ἑαυτῶν ἐξῆλθον εἰς ὑπάντησιν τοῦ νυμφίου.
paragraphs.translit: Tote homoiōthēsetai hē basileia tōn ouranōn deka parthenois, haitines labousai tas lampadas heautōn exēlthon eis hypantēsin tou nymphiou.

i18n.en: Then the kingdom of the heavens will be likened to ten virgins, who took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom.

notes.official: **The Ten Virgins parable opens.** *Tote homoiōthēsetai hē basileia tōn ouranōn deka parthenois* — 'then the kingdom of the heavens will be likened to ten virgins'. The kingdom-similitude formula introduces the eschatological parable-pair (Ten Virgins + Talents) that closes the eschatological-discourse (Mt 23-25) before the Sheep-and-Goats final-judgment. The bridegroom-figure echoes the Hebrew Bible YHWH-as-bridegroom tradition (Hos 2; Isa 54:5; Jer 2:2). See `kingdom-of-heaven-basileia-tōn-ouranōn-mt-distinctive-cross-corpus-hebrew-malkhut-shamayim`.

paragraphs.text: πέντε δὲ ἐξ αὐτῶν ἦσαν μωραὶ καὶ πέντε φρόνιμοι.
paragraphs.translit: pente de ex autōn ēsan mōrai kai pente phronimoi.

i18n.en: And five of them were foolish, and five were prudent.

paragraphs.text: αἱ γὰρ μωραὶ λαβοῦσαι τὰς λαμπάδας αὐτῶν οὐκ ἔλαβον μεθ' ἑαυτῶν ἔλαιον·
paragraphs.translit: hai gar mōrai labousai tas lampadas autōn ouk elabon meth' heautōn elaion·

i18n.en: For the foolish, when they took their lamps, took no oil with them;

paragraphs.text: αἱ δὲ φρόνιμοι ἔλαβον ἔλαιον ἐν τοῖς ἀγγείοις μετὰ τῶν λαμπάδων ἑαυτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: hai de phronimoi elabon elaion en tois angeiois meta tōn lampadōn heautōn.

i18n.en: but the prudent took oil in their flasks along with their lamps.

paragraphs.text: χρονίζοντος δὲ τοῦ νυμφίου ἐνύσταξαν πᾶσαι καὶ ἐκάθευδον.
paragraphs.translit: chronizontos de tou nymphiou enystaxan pasai kai ekatheudon.

i18n.en: And while the bridegroom was delayed, they all became drowsy and slept.

paragraphs.text: μέσης δὲ νυκτὸς κραυγὴ γέγονεν· Ἰδοὺ ὁ νυμφίος, ἐξέρχεσθε εἰς ἀπάντησιν.
paragraphs.translit: mesēs de nyktos kraugē gegonen· Idou ho nymphios, exerchesthe eis apantēsin.

i18n.en: But at midnight there came a cry: "Behold, the bridegroom! Come out to meet him."

paragraphs.text: τότε ἠγέρθησαν πᾶσαι αἱ παρθένοι ἐκεῖναι καὶ ἐκόσμησαν τὰς λαμπάδας ἑαυτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: tote ēgerthēsan pasai hai parthenoi ekeinai kai ekosmēsan tas lampadas heautōn.

i18n.en: Then all those virgins rose and trimmed their lamps.

paragraphs.text: αἱ δὲ μωραὶ ταῖς φρονίμοις εἶπαν· Δότε ἡμῖν ἐκ τοῦ ἐλαίου ὑμῶν, ὅτι αἱ λαμπάδες ἡμῶν σβέννυνται.
paragraphs.translit: hai de mōrai tais phronimois eipan· Dote hēmin ek tou elaiou hymōn, hoti hai lampades hēmōn sbennyntai.

i18n.en: And the foolish said to the prudent, "Give us some of your oil, for our lamps are going out."

paragraphs.text: ἀπεκρίθησαν δὲ αἱ φρόνιμοι λέγουσαι· Μήποτε οὐ μὴ ἀρκέσῃ ἡμῖν καὶ ὑμῖν· πορεύεσθε μᾶλλον πρὸς τοὺς πωλοῦντας καὶ ἀγοράσατε ἑαυταῖς.
paragraphs.translit: apekrithēsan de hai phronimoi legousai· Mēpote ou mē arkesē hēmin kai hymin· poreuesthe mallon pros tous pōlountas kai agorasate heautais.

i18n.en: But the prudent answered, saying, "There will not be enough for us and for you. Go rather to those who sell and buy for yourselves."

paragraphs.text: ἀπερχομένων δὲ αὐτῶν ἀγοράσαι ἦλθεν ὁ νυμφίος, καὶ αἱ ἕτοιμοι εἰσῆλθον μετ' αὐτοῦ εἰς τοὺς γάμους, καὶ ἐκλείσθη ἡ θύρα.
paragraphs.translit: aperchomenōn de autōn agorasai ēlthen ho nymphios, kai hai hetoimoi eisēlthon met' autou eis tous gamous, kai ekleisthē hē thyra.

i18n.en: And while they were going off to buy, the bridegroom came, and those who were ready went in with him to the wedding feast, and the door was shut.

paragraphs.text: ὕστερον δὲ ἔρχονται καὶ αἱ λοιπαὶ παρθένοι λέγουσαι· Κύριε κύριε, ἄνοιξον ἡμῖν.
paragraphs.translit: hysteron de erchontai kai hai loipai parthenoi legousai· Kyrie kyrie, anoixon hēmin.

i18n.en: Later, the other virgins also came, saying, "Lord, lord, open to us."

paragraphs.text: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, οὐκ οἶδα ὑμᾶς.
paragraphs.translit: ho de apokritheis eipen· Amēn legō hymin, ouk oida hymas.

i18n.en: But he answered, saying, "Amen I say to you, I do not know you."

paragraphs.text: γρηγορεῖτε οὖν, ὅτι οὐκ οἴδατε τὴν ἡμέραν οὐδὲ τὴν ὥραν.
paragraphs.translit: grēgoreite oun, hoti ouk oidate tēn hēmeran oude tēn hōran.

i18n.en: Keep watch, therefore, for you know neither the day nor the hour.

notes.official: *grēgoreite oun, hoti ouk oidate tēn hēmeran oude tēn hōran* — 'keep watch, therefore, for you do not know the day or the hour'. The eschatological-vigilance theme; Mt 24:42, 44, 50; Mk 13:33; the *grēgoreite* watchword.

paragraphs.text: Ὥσπερ γὰρ ἄνθρωπος ἀποδημῶν ἐκάλεσεν τοὺς ἰδίους δούλους καὶ παρέδωκεν αὐτοῖς τὰ ὑπάρχοντα αὐτοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: Hōsper gar anthrōpos apodēmōn ekalesen tous idious doulous kai paredōken autois ta hyparchonta autou,

i18n.en: For it is just as when a man going on a journey called his own servants and entrusted to them his possessions.

notes.official: **The Talents parable opens.** Synoptic-parallel: Lk 19:11-27 (the more-elaborate Lukan minas-parable). The *talanton* — a large weight-measure of silver, ~6,000 denarii or ~20 years of laborer-wages. The parable's accounting-figures are deliberately enormous.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ᾧ μὲν ἔδωκεν πέντε τάλαντα ᾧ δὲ δύο ᾧ δὲ ἕν, ἑκάστῳ κατὰ τὴν ἰδίαν δύναμιν, καὶ ἀπεδήμησεν. εὐθέως
paragraphs.translit: kai hō men edōken pente talanta hō de dyo hō de hen, hekastō kata tēn idian dynamin, kai apedēmēsen. eutheōs

i18n.en: And to one he gave five talents, to another two, and to another one, to each according to his own ability; and he went on his journey. At once

paragraphs.text: πορευθεὶς ὁ τὰ πέντε τάλαντα λαβὼν ἠργάσατο ἐν αὐτοῖς καὶ ἐκέρδησεν ἄλλα πέντε·
paragraphs.translit: poreutheis ho ta pente talanta labōn ērgasato en autois kai ekerdēsen alla pente·

i18n.en: the one who had received the five talents went and traded with them and gained another five.

paragraphs.text: ὡσαύτως ὁ τὰ δύο ἐκέρδησεν ἄλλα δύο·
paragraphs.translit: hōsautōs ho ta dyo ekerdēsen alla dyo·

i18n.en: Likewise the one who had the two gained another two.

paragraphs.text: ὁ δὲ τὸ ἓν λαβὼν ἀπελθὼν ὤρυξεν γῆν καὶ ἔκρυψεν τὸ ἀργύριον τοῦ κυρίου αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: ho de to hen labōn apelthōn ōryxen gēn kai ekrypsen to argyrion tou kyriou autou.

i18n.en: But the one who had received the one went off and dug in the ground and hid his master's silver.

paragraphs.text: μετὰ δὲ πολὺν χρόνον ἔρχεται ὁ κύριος τῶν δούλων ἐκείνων καὶ συναίρει λόγον μετ' αὐτῶν
paragraphs.translit: meta de polyn chronon erchetai ho kyrios tōn doulōn ekeinōn kai synairei logon met' autōn

i18n.en: Now after a long time the master of those servants came and settled accounts with them.

paragraphs.text: καὶ προσελθὼν ὁ τὰ πέντε τάλαντα λαβὼν προσήνεγκεν ἄλλα πέντε τάλαντα λέγων· Κύριε, πέντε τάλαντά μοι παρέδωκας· ἴδε ἄλλα πέντε τάλαντα ἐκέρδησα.
paragraphs.translit: kai proselthōn ho ta pente talanta labōn prosēnegken alla pente talanta legōn· Kyrie, pente talanta moi paredōkas· ide alla pente talanta ekerdēsa.

i18n.en: And the one who had received the five talents came forward and brought another five talents, saying, "Master, you entrusted to me five talents; see, I have gained another five talents."

paragraphs.text: ἔφη αὐτῷ ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ· Εὖ, δοῦλε ἀγαθὲ καὶ πιστέ, ἐπὶ ὀλίγα ἦς πιστός, ἐπὶ πολλῶν σε καταστήσω· εἴσελθε εἰς τὴν χαρὰν τοῦ κυρίου σου.
paragraphs.translit: ephē autō ho kyrios autou· Eu, doule agathe kai piste, epi oliga ēs pistos, epi pollōn se katastēsō· eiselthe eis tēn charan tou kyriou sou.

i18n.en: His master said to him, "Well done, good and faithful servant. You have been faithful over a few things; I will set you over many. Enter into the joy of your master."

notes.official: *eu, doule agathe kai piste ... eiselthe eis tēn charan tou kyriou sou* — 'well done, good and faithful servant ... enter into the joy of your lord'. The reward-formula; cross-corpus to Jewish-apocalyptic reward-of-the-righteous (1 Enoch 39:3-14; T. Levi 18; 4 Ezra 7).

paragraphs.text: προσελθὼν δὲ καὶ ὁ τὰ δύο τάλαντα εἶπεν· Κύριε, δύο τάλαντά μοι παρέδωκας· ἴδε ἄλλα δύο τάλαντα ἐκέρδησα.
paragraphs.translit: proselthōn de kai ho ta dyo talanta eipen· Kyrie, dyo talanta moi paredōkas· ide alla dyo talanta ekerdēsa.

i18n.en: The one who had received the two talents also came forward and said, "Master, you entrusted to me two talents; see, I have gained another two talents."

paragraphs.text: ἔφη αὐτῷ ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ· Εὖ, δοῦλε ἀγαθὲ καὶ πιστέ, ἐπὶ ὀλίγα ἦς πιστός, ἐπὶ πολλῶν σε καταστήσω· εἴσελθε εἰς τὴν χαρὰν τοῦ κυρίου σου.
paragraphs.translit: ephē autō ho kyrios autou· Eu, doule agathe kai piste, epi oliga ēs pistos, epi pollōn se katastēsō· eiselthe eis tēn charan tou kyriou sou.

i18n.en: His master said to him, "Well done, good and faithful servant. You have been faithful over a few things; I will set you over many. Enter into the joy of your master."

paragraphs.text: προσελθὼν δὲ καὶ ὁ τὸ ἓν τάλαντον εἰληφὼς εἶπεν· Κύριε, ἔγνων σε ὅτι σκληρὸς εἶ ἄνθρωπος, θερίζων ὅπου οὐκ ἔσπειρας καὶ συνάγων ὅθεν οὐ διεσκόρπισας·
paragraphs.translit: proselthōn de kai ho to hen talanton eilēphōs eipen· Kyrie, egnōn se hoti sklēros ei anthrōpos, therizōn hopou ouk espeiras kai synagōn hothen ou dieskorpisas·

i18n.en: Then the one who had received the one talent also came forward and said, "Master, I knew you to be a hard man, reaping where you did not sow and gathering where you did not scatter;

paragraphs.text: καὶ φοβηθεὶς ἀπελθὼν ἔκρυψα τὸ τάλαντόν σου ἐν τῇ γῇ· ἴδε ἔχεις τὸ σόν.
paragraphs.translit: kai phobētheis apelthōn ekrypsa to talanton sou en tē gē· ide echeis to son.

i18n.en: and being afraid, I went and hid your talent in the ground. See, you have what is yours."

paragraphs.text: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Πονηρὲ δοῦλε καὶ ὀκνηρέ, ᾔδεις ὅτι θερίζω ὅπου οὐκ ἔσπειρα καὶ συνάγω ὅθεν οὐ διεσκόρπισα;
paragraphs.translit: apokritheis de ho kyrios autou eipen autō· Ponēre doule kai oknēre, ēdeis hoti therizō hopou ouk espeira kai synagō hothen ou dieskorpisa;

i18n.en: But his master answered him, saying, "Wicked and slothful servant! You knew that I reap where I did not sow and gather where I did not scatter?

paragraphs.text: ἔδει σε οὖν βαλεῖν τὰ ἀργύριά μου τοῖς τραπεζίταις, καὶ ἐλθὼν ἐγὼ ἐκομισάμην ἂν τὸ ἐμὸν σὺν τόκῳ.
paragraphs.translit: edei se oun balein ta argyria mou tois trapezitais, kai elthōn egō ekomisamēn an to emon syn tokō.

i18n.en: You ought, then, to have put my silver with the bankers, and on my coming I would have received back what was mine with interest.

paragraphs.text: ἄρατε οὖν ἀπ' αὐτοῦ τὸ τάλαντον καὶ δότε τῷ ἔχοντι τὰ δέκα τάλαντα·
paragraphs.translit: arate oun ap' autou to talanton kai dote tō echonti ta deka talanta·

i18n.en: Take therefore the talent from him and give it to the one who has the ten talents.

paragraphs.text: τῷ γὰρ ἔχοντι παντὶ δοθήσεται καὶ περισσευθήσεται· τοῦ δὲ μὴ ἔχοντος καὶ ὃ ἔχει ἀρθήσεται ἀπ' αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: tō gar echonti panti dothēsetai kai perisseuthēsetai· tou de mē echontos kai ho echei arthēsetai ap' autou.

i18n.en: For to everyone who has, more will be given, and he will have abundance; but from the one who has not, even what he has will be taken away.

paragraphs.text: καὶ τὸν ἀχρεῖον δοῦλον ἐκβάλετε εἰς τὸ σκότος τὸ ἐξώτερον· ἐκεῖ ἔσται ὁ κλαυθμὸς καὶ ὁ βρυγμὸς τῶν ὀδόντων.
paragraphs.translit: kai ton achreion doulon ekbalete eis to skotos to exōteron· ekei estai ho klauthmos kai ho brygmos tōn odontōn.

i18n.en: And cast the useless servant into the outer darkness; there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth."

notes.official: *to skotos to exōteron; ekei estai ho klauthmos kai ho brygmos tōn odontōn* — 'the outer darkness; there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth'. The Matthean-distinctive apocalyptic-judgment formula (also at Mt 8:12; 13:42; 13:50; 22:13; 24:51).

paragraphs.text: Ὅταν δὲ ἔλθῃ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐν τῇ δόξῃ αὐτοῦ καὶ πάντες οἱ ἄγγελοι μετ' αὐτοῦ, τότε καθίσει ἐπὶ θρόνου δόξης αὐτοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: Hotan de elthē ho huios tou anthrōpou en tē doxē autou kai pantes hoi angeloi met' autou, tote kathisei epi thronou doxēs autou·

i18n.en: When the Son of Man comes in his glory, and all the angels with him, then he will sit on the throne of his glory.

notes.official: **The Sheep-and-Goats Final Judgment opens.** *Hotan de elthē ho huios tou anthrōpou en tē doxē autou kai pantes hoi angeloi met' autou, tote kathisei epi thronou doxēs autou* — 'when the Son of Man comes in his glory, and all the angels with him, then he will sit on his glorious throne'. Direct appropriation of Dan 7:13-14 LXX: the *thronos doxēs* echoes Dan 7:9 enthronement; angels-attending echoes Dan 7:10; universal-judgment role echoes Dan 7:14. See `son-of-man-bar-enash-dan-7-13-mt-cross-corpus` and `sheep-and-goats-mt-25-31-46-adelphōn-mou-tōn-elachistōn-three-readings-gray-cross-corpus`.

paragraphs.text: καὶ συναχθήσονται ἔμπροσθεν αὐτοῦ πάντα τὰ ἔθνη, καὶ ἀφορίσει αὐτοὺς ἀπ' ἀλλήλων, ὥσπερ ὁ ποιμὴν ἀφορίζει τὰ πρόβατα ἀπὸ τῶν ἐρίφων,
paragraphs.translit: kai synachthēsontai emprosthen autou panta ta ethnē, kai aphorisei autous ap' allēlōn, hōsper ho poimēn aphorizei ta probata apo tōn eriphōn,

i18n.en: And all the nations will be gathered before him, and he will separate them one from another as the shepherd separates the sheep from the goats.

notes.official: *synachthēsontai emprosthen autou panta ta ethnē* — 'all the nations will be gathered before him'. *panta ta ethnē* admits both the universalist 'all peoples including Israel' and the strict 'all the Gentile-nations' readings (Hare/Harrington 1975 vs Meier 1977). Cross-corpus to Joel 3:11-12 (the eschatological-judgment-of-the-nations).

paragraphs.text: καὶ στήσει τὰ μὲν πρόβατα ἐκ δεξιῶν αὐτοῦ τὰ δὲ ἐρίφια ἐξ εὐωνύμων.
paragraphs.translit: kai stēsei ta men probata ek dexiōn autou ta de eriphia ex euōnymōn.

i18n.en: And he will set the sheep at his right hand, and the goats at the left.

notes.official: Sheep-and-goats sorting-image. Cross-corpus to Ezek 34:17-22 (the eschatological-sorting-of-the-flock prophecy).

paragraphs.text: τότε ἐρεῖ ὁ βασιλεὺς τοῖς ἐκ δεξιῶν αὐτοῦ· Δεῦτε, οἱ εὐλογημένοι τοῦ πατρός μου, κληρονομήσατε τὴν ἡτοιμασμένην ὑμῖν βασιλείαν ἀπὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου.
paragraphs.translit: tote erei ho basileus tois ek dexiōn autou· Deute, hoi eulogēmenoi tou patros mou, klēronomēsate tēn hētoimasmenēn hymin basileian apo katabolēs kosmou.

i18n.en: Then the king will say to those at his right hand, "Come, you who are blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world.

notes.official: *deute hoi eulogēmenoi tou patros mou, klēronomēsate tēn hētoimasmenēn hymin basileian apo katabolēs kosmou* — 'come, you blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world'. The kingdom-as-inheritance from-the-foundation-of-the-world echoes Jewish-apocalyptic pre-existent-creation themes (4 Ezra 8:52; 2 Bar 4:3).

paragraphs.text: ἐπείνασα γὰρ καὶ ἐδώκατέ μοι φαγεῖν, ἐδίψησα καὶ ἐποτίσατέ με, ξένος ἤμην καὶ συνηγάγετέ με,
paragraphs.translit: epeinasa gar kai edōkate moi phagein, edipsēsa kai epotisate me, xenos ēmēn kai synēgagete me,

i18n.en: For I was hungry and you gave me food; I was thirsty and you gave me drink; I was a stranger and you took me in;

notes.official: **The six-fold acts-of-mercy list** (vv.35-36). Hungry-fed / thirsty-given-drink / stranger-welcomed / naked-clothed / sick-visited / imprisoned-visited. Cross-corpus to Isa 58:6-10 (the prophetic critique-of-fasting + acts-of-mercy program); Job 22:6-7; T. Iss. 7:5; T. Jos. 1:5-7; m.Sotah 14a (the rabbinic *gemilut ḥasadim* tradition). The Matthean Final-Judgment criterion is rooted in Jewish-mercy tradition.

paragraphs.text: γυμνὸς καὶ περιεβάλετέ με, ἠσθένησα καὶ ἐπεσκέψασθέ με, ἐν φυλακῇ ἤμην καὶ ἤλθατε πρός με.
paragraphs.translit: gymnos kai periebalete me, ēsthenēsa kai epeskepsasthe me, en phylakē ēmēn kai ēlthate pros me.

i18n.en: naked and you clothed me; I was sick and you visited me; I was in prison and you came to me."

paragraphs.text: τότε ἀποκριθήσονται αὐτῷ οἱ δίκαιοι λέγοντες· Κύριε, πότε σε εἴδομεν πεινῶντα καὶ ἐθρέψαμεν, ἢ διψῶντα καὶ ἐποτίσαμεν;
paragraphs.translit: tote apokrithēsontai autō hoi dikaioi legontes· Kyrie, pote se eidomen peinōnta kai ethrepsamen, ē dipsōnta kai epotisamen;

i18n.en: Then the righteous will answer him, saying, "Lord, when did we see you hungry and feed you, or thirsty and give you drink?

paragraphs.text: πότε δέ σε εἴδομεν ξένον καὶ συνηγάγομεν, ἢ γυμνὸν καὶ περιεβάλομεν;
paragraphs.translit: pote de se eidomen xenon kai synēgagomen, ē gymnon kai periebalomen;

i18n.en: And when did we see you a stranger and take you in, or naked and clothe you?

paragraphs.text: πότε δέ σε εἴδομεν ἀσθενοῦντα ἢ ἐν φυλακῇ καὶ ἤλθομεν πρός σε;
paragraphs.translit: pote de se eidomen asthenounta ē en phylakē kai ēlthomen pros se;

i18n.en: And when did we see you sick or in prison and come to you?"

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ βασιλεὺς ἐρεῖ αὐτοῖς· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἐφ' ὅσον ἐποιήσατε ἑνὶ τούτων τῶν ἀδελφῶν μου τῶν ἐλαχίστων, ἐμοὶ ἐποιήσατε.
paragraphs.translit: kai apokritheis ho basileus erei autois· Amēn legō hymin, eph' hoson epoiēsate heni toutōn tōn adelphōn mou tōn elachistōn, emoi epoiēsate.

i18n.en: And the king will answer them, saying, "Amen I say to you, inasmuch as you did it to one of the least of these my brothers, you did it to me."

notes.official: **The central crux.** *eph' hoson epoiēsate heni toutōn tōn adelphōn mou tōn elachistōn, emoi epoiēsate* — 'inasmuch as you did it to one of the least of these my brothers, you did it to me'. The *adelphōn mou tōn elachistōn* identification-question is the load-bearing interpretive-site. Gray 1989 identifies three reading-strata: (1) universalist (= all suffering humanity); (2) restricted-Christian-missionary (= the disciple-band, cf. Mt 10:42); (3) restricted-Christian-brethren (= the suffering-poor-among-Christians). All three readings have substantial-textual warrant; the philological data does not by itself decide. The WoH-Translation preserves the literal 'brothers' rendering and documents all three readings in `sheep-and-goats-mt-25-31-46-adelphōn-mou-tōn-elachistōn-three-readings-gray-cross-corpus`. Note the textual-asymmetry with v.45 (which lacks *adelphōn mou*) — see overlay entry `adelphōn-mou-presence-absence-asymmetry-mt-25-40-vs-25-45-gray`.

paragraphs.text: Τότε ἐρεῖ καὶ τοῖς ἐξ εὐωνύμων· Πορεύεσθε ἀπ' ἐμοῦ κατηραμένοι εἰς τὸ πῦρ τὸ αἰώνιον τὸ ἡτοιμασμένον τῷ διαβόλῳ καὶ τοῖς ἀγγέλοις αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: Tote erei kai tois ex euōnymōn· Poreuesthe ap' emou katēramenoi eis to pyr to aiōnion to hētoimasmenon tō diabolō kai tois angelois autou.

i18n.en: Then he will say also to those at the left, "Depart from me, you cursed, into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels.

notes.official: *to pyr to aiōnion to hētoimasmenon tō diabolō kai tois angelois autou* — 'the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels'. *aiōnios* — the philological-breadth question: 'endless-eternal' (KJV/RSV/NRSV/NIV) vs 'age-pertaining' (Hart 2017 et al.). Cross-corpus to 1 Enoch 90:24-27 (apocalyptic fire-of-judgment for the fallen-angels); Jub 24:30; Rev 20:10, 14-15. The WoH-Translation preserves 'eternal' per the dominant English-tradition convention and documents the breadth in `aiōnios-mt-25-41-46-eternal-vs-age-pertaining-cross-corpus` + overlay `aionios-eternal-vs-age-pertaining-translation-convention`.

paragraphs.text: ἐπείνασα γὰρ καὶ οὐκ ἐδώκατέ μοι φαγεῖν, ἐδίψησα καὶ οὐκ ἐποτίσατέ με,
paragraphs.translit: epeinasa gar kai ouk edōkate moi phagein, edipsēsa kai ouk epotisate me,

i18n.en: For I was hungry and you gave me no food; I was thirsty and you gave me no drink;

paragraphs.text: ξένος ἤμην καὶ οὐ συνηγάγετέ με, γυμνὸς καὶ οὐ περιεβάλετέ με, ἀσθενὴς καὶ ἐν φυλακῇ καὶ οὐκ ἐπεσκέψασθέ με.
paragraphs.translit: xenos ēmēn kai ou synēgagete me, gymnos kai ou periebalete me, asthenēs kai en phylakē kai ouk epeskepsasthe me.

i18n.en: I was a stranger and you did not take me in; naked and you did not clothe me; sick and in prison and you did not visit me."

paragraphs.text: τότε ἀποκριθήσονται καὶ αὐτοὶ λέγοντες· Κύριε, πότε σε εἴδομεν πεινῶντα ἢ διψῶντα ἢ ξένον ἢ γυμνὸν ἢ ἀσθενῆ ἢ ἐν φυλακῇ καὶ οὐ διηκονήσαμέν σοι;
paragraphs.translit: tote apokrithēsontai kai autoi legontes· Kyrie, pote se eidomen peinōnta ē dipsōnta ē xenon ē gymnon ē asthenē ē en phylakē kai ou diēkonēsamen soi;

i18n.en: Then they also will answer, saying, "Lord, when did we see you hungry or thirsty or a stranger or naked or sick or in prison and did not serve you?"

paragraphs.text: τότε ἀποκριθήσεται αὐτοῖς λέγων· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἐφ' ὅσον οὐκ ἐποιήσατε ἑνὶ τούτων τῶν ἐλαχίστων, οὐδὲ ἐμοὶ ἐποιήσατε.
paragraphs.translit: tote apokrithēsetai autois legōn· Amēn legō hymin, eph' hoson ouk epoiēsate heni toutōn tōn elachistōn, oude emoi epoiēsate.

i18n.en: Then he will answer them, saying, "Amen I say to you, inasmuch as you did not do it to one of the least of these, neither did you do it to me."

notes.official: **Textual asymmetry.** *eph' hoson ouk epoiēsate heni toutōn tōn elachistōn, oude emoi epoiēsate* — 'inasmuch as you did it not to one of the least of these, you did it not to me'. NOTE: v.45 LACKS *adelphōn mou* present at v.40. The asymmetry is preserved per Gray 1989. Implications for the universalist-vs-restricted reading-debate are documented in overlay entry `adelphōn-mou-presence-absence-asymmetry-mt-25-40-vs-25-45-gray`.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἀπελεύσονται οὗτοι εἰς κόλασιν αἰώνιον, οἱ δὲ δίκαιοι εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον.
paragraphs.translit: kai apeleusontai houtoi eis kolasin aiōnion, hoi de dikaioi eis zōēn aiōnion.

i18n.en: And these will go away into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life.

notes.official: *kai apeleusontai houtoi eis kolasin aiōnion, hoi de dikaioi eis zōēn aiōnion* — 'and these will go away into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life'. **The Matthean parallel-structure** *kolasin aiōnion / zōēn aiōnion*. The parallel-structure argument: if *aiōnion* in 'eternal life' means 'endless-eternal', then *aiōnion* in 'eternal punishment' must equally. The conditionalist counter-argument: parallelism does not require identical-semantic-content. The WoH-Translation preserves 'eternal' on the surface; see `aiōnios-mt-25-41-46-eternal-vs-age-pertaining-cross-corpus`.

editorial_questions_resolved: All 14 editorial questions resolved in the 2026-06-04 editor pass (claude-opus-4-7). Each question folded into a glossary entry (central or overlay) or into per-verse commentary documenting the philological, textual-critical, and cross-corpus considerations; defaults were preserved per the standard ASV/RSV scholarly-translation baseline. See per-paragraph `commentary` fields and the central glossary entries listed in `glossaryRefs[]` for full philological treatment.
